also: separate the yolk from the white

terms.grammar: dissolvō, dissolvere, dissolvī, dissolūtum, with ōva
evidence: Apic. 4.2.15: ōva cōnfringēs in caccabum et dissolvēs
Apic. 2.1.5: adjiciēs ōva quīnque et dissolvēs dīligenter, ut ūnum corpus efficiās
terms.comment: Apicius’s phrase, many times over: dissolvere, classically to loosen or break up, of eggs beaten until they run together into one. He also says agitāre, to stir or shake: frangēs ōva VIII et agitābis. See “whip”.

terms.grammar: frangō, frangere, frēgī, frāctum, with ōva; also cōnfringere
evidence: Apic. 4.2.36: frangēs ōva VIII et agitābis
terms.comment: Apicius has both frangere and cōnfringere. Of breaking into an egg at table, Petronius says pertundere, to pierce: see the examples.

terms.gloss: separate the white from the yolk
evidence: Cels. 6.6.1: ōvī album in vās (Lewis & Short s.v. dēfundō)
terms.comment: A description of ours in classical words (sēcernere, put apart; album ōvī; vitellus): we have found no set phrase for separating eggs. Celsus has the white poured off into a vessel, ōvī album in vās dēfundere.

phrases.latin: ōva cōnfringēs in caccabum et dissolvēs
phrases.english: crack the eggs into the pot and beat them
crack eight eggs and beat them
You crack the eggs, and I’ll beat them.
Carefully separate the white from the yolk.

phrases.latin: ōvaque ex farīnā pinguī figūrāta pertundimus
phrases.english: and we broke open the eggs, which were made of rich pastry

phrases.latin: Albūmina in catīnum siccum mitte et agitā, dōnec spūmās agant.
phrases.english: Put the whites in a dry bowl and beat them until they foam.
